solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Also pocketing catch on West Indian island …

indicators.note: pocketing means the first word swallows the second, holding it inside like a pocket

parts.note: also means too
to catch is to bag, as a hunter bags game

explanation.surface: A fisherman on a Caribbean island also lands a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue into 4-across, whose answer partners this island in one nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is one of the two main islands of the Caribbean state of Trinidad and Tobago.

clue.text: Battle-ship contest?

parts.note: read as a towing boat (a ship) plus a phrase meaning battle, it names a rope-pulling contest between two teams

explanation.surface: A naval contest between warships.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope-pulling contest whose name joins a kind of boat with a word for battle.

clue.text: Ointment spoken of at castle

parts.note: balm is a soothing ointment
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: A soothing cream gets talked about up at the castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Balmoral is the British royal family's castle in Aberdeenshire, Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral is a royal castle in Scotland, a summer residence of the British monarch.

clue.text: Poet at French wine region

definitions.meaning: Robert ..., English poet and author of I, Claudius
a district south of Bordeaux known for red and white wines

explanation.surface: A poet visits a French wine region.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Graves was a poet, and the Graves district near Bordeaux is a wine region.

clue.text: … partnering Chinese secret society accepting new identity

indicators.note: accepting means the society takes the other letters in, holding them within

parts.note: a triad is a Chinese secret society, often criminal
ID is the usual short form of identity

explanation.surface: Someone joining a Chinese gang is given a fresh identity.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 1-across: the definition is the island that partners Tobago.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinidad is the larger island joined with Tobago in the twin-island Caribbean republic.

clue.text: It's steady to be unsteady

definitions.meaning: something firm and dependable, like a solid stone support

explanation.surface: A paradox: being steady means being unsteady.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock is a byword for steadiness, while to rock is to sway unsteadily.

clue.text: Location of US university when rebuilt has shortened road

indicators.note: rebuilt means the letters of when are reassembled in a new order
shortened means the road word loses its final letters

parts.note: an avenue is a road

explanation.surface: An American campus town has been rebuilt with a truncated road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' makes NEWH from WHEN; 'shortened' cuts AVENUE to AVEN; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: New Haven, Connecticut is home to Yale University.

clue.text: Inward characters of Australian city

indicators.note: the characters, or letters, of the word are used in another order

explanation.surface: Introspective traits of a city Down Under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters of' asks for the letters of INWARD rearranged to give DARWIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Darwin is the capital of Australia's Northern Territory.

clue.text: Sandhill around some French city

indicators.note: around means the sandhill word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a dune is a sandhill
de is the French for some, as in du pain or de l'eau

explanation.surface: A sand dune surrounds a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: Dundee is a city in Scotland, not France; 'French' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Dundee is a city on the east coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Leading grammarian for ever cut short at Irish city

indicators.note: leading means the opening letter of grammarian
cut short means the final letter is removed

parts.note: always means for ever

explanation.surface: A top grammarian, his career eternally curtailed, ends up in an Irish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Galway is a city on the west coast of Ireland.

clue.text: Unsettled winchers at capital of German Land

indicators.note: unsettled means the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Restless crane operators in a German state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: A German Land is one of Germany's federal states.
explanation.definitionFit: Schwerin is the capital of the German state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.

clue.text: Detained in religious group out east on river

indicators.note: in means the detained word sits inside the reduced group word
out means the letter for east is dropped from the religious group

parts.note: a sect is a religious group
held means detained

explanation.surface: Someone held by a religious sect escapes east by river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scheldt is a river flowing through France, Belgium and the Netherlands to the North Sea.

clue.text: Rolf returning in this French city

indicators.note: returning means the name is read backwards

parts.note: en is French for in and ce is French for this

explanation.surface: Rolf coming back to a city in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' applies to 'in this', giving EN CE; the city is Italian, though Florence is its French and English name.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence is the Tuscan city known in Italian as Firenze.

clue.text: French dramatist who could be in care in Wisconsin

indicators.note: could be means these letters may form another word once rearranged

explanation.surface: A French playwright who might end up in care in Wisconsin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Wisconsin' adds a second hint: Racine is also a city in Wisconsin.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Racine was a seventeenth-century French tragedian, author of Phèdre.

clue.text: Knight on a broken chair in city in Pakistan

parts.note: K is the chess notation for knight

indicators.note: broken means the letters of chair are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A knight sits on a broken chair in a Pakistani city.
explanation.definitionFit: Karachi is Pakistan's largest city and main seaport.

clue.text: Some peculiar antiquities from islands near 9

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some odd antiques come from islands off Galway.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition dropped 9; the islands lie near 9-across, Galway, and 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aran Islands lie at the mouth of Galway Bay off western Ireland.

clue.text: Live in the Scottish mountains in Hindu holy city

indicators.note: in means the living word sits inside the mountains word

parts.note: bens are Scottish mountains, as in Ben Nevis
are, as in they are, means they live or exist

explanation.surface: Dwelling in the Highlands, in a sacred Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Benares, now Varanasi, is the holiest city of Hinduism on the Ganges.

clue.text: Showy state

parts.note: read as a state that is also a show, it is a US state sharing its name with a Rodgers and Hammerstein musical

explanation.surface: A flashy state.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state whose name is also the title of a famous stage musical.

clue.text: US shade over a party in state

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the rest

parts.note: color is the American spelling of colour, a shade
a do is a party

explanation.surface: An American hue hangs over a state party.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado is a western US state.

clue.text: Priest leaving press crossing to town in Lincolnshire

indicators.note: leaving means the priest letter departs from the press word

parts.note: to stamp is to press down
a ford is a river crossing

explanation.surface: A priest quits the newspapers for a crossing to a market town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like the newspapers, but it is the verb stamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamford is a historic market town in Lincolnshire, England.

clue.text: Small child kicking over pile on Cumbrian mountain

parts.note: a kid is a child

indicators.note: kicking over means the pile word is knocked backwards

parts.note: a wad is a pile, as of banknotes

explanation.surface: A small child kicks over a heap on a Lake District peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiddaw is a mountain in the Lake District in Cumbria, northwest England.

clue.text: Otterden on the Dee south of Chester

definitions.meaning: the den or lair of an otter

definitions.text: on the Dee south of Chester
definitions.meaning: a Welsh village on the River Dee just south of the English city of Chester

explanation.surface: An otter's den on the River Dee below Chester.
explanation.definitionFit: A holt is an otter's lair, and Holt is a village in Wrexham on the Dee.

clue.text: Somewhat upset, people practising, organ

indicators.note: upset says the hidden letters are read backwards
Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Musicians practising on the organ get somewhat upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the instrument; here it is a flower part.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpel is the female reproductive organ of a flower.

clue.text: Erasmus endlessly confused in African capital

indicators.note: confused means the remaining letters are jumbled
endlessly means the final letter is removed

explanation.surface: The scholar Erasmus, forever muddled, in an African capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts ERASMUS to ERASMU; 'confused' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Maseru is the capital city of Lesotho.

clue.text: Scottish loch could be lake. Right!

indicators.note: could be means these letters may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A Scottish loch might be a lake, quite right!
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram pool is LAKE plus RT, the abbreviation for 'Right'.
explanation.definitionFit: Loch Arklet is a small loch in the Trossachs of Scotland.

clue.text: First prohibition involving notice at African capital

annotationWithheld.why: First prohibition involving notice at African capital (6): wordplay gives A + BAN round AD, but Abadan is an Iranian port, not an African capital, so the definition is wrong for the answer.
annotationWithheld.clue: First prohibition involving notice at African capital

clue.text: Vehicle grave, reportedly, in African capital

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a car is a vehicle and a tomb a grave

explanation.surface: A vehicle as a grave, so the story goes, in an African capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Khartoum is the capital of Sudan, at the meeting of the Blue and White Nile.

clue.text: Animal from the outer parts of Lisbon

indicators.note: only the outer parts of the city name are kept, the central letters falling away

explanation.surface: A beast from the edges of Lisbon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the outer parts of' keeps the first two and last two letters of LISBON, dropping SB.
explanation.definitionFit: The lion is a large wild cat, the king of beasts.

clue.text: A pierrot dancing in African capital

indicators.note: dancing means the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A clown dancing in an African capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretoria is the administrative capital of South Africa.

clue.text: Fruit with no core sent back, therefore, to Texan city

indicators.note: sent back means the cored fruit is read in reverse
with no core means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: an apple is a fruit
so means therefore

explanation.surface: A cored apple is returned, and so off to a city in Texas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no core' cuts APPLE to APLE; 'sent back' turns it into ELPA.
explanation.definitionFit: El Paso is a city in west Texas on the Rio Grande.

clue.text: Girl lost shilling in country road in Swiss city

indicators.note: in means the reduced name sits inside the road word

parts.note: a lane is a narrow country road

indicators.note: lost means the shilling letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Susan is a girl's name
S was the abbreviation for the old British shilling

explanation.surface: A girl drops a shilling on a country lane in a Swiss city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl' looks like the definition but supplies the name. The shilling was an old British coin worth a twentieth of a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Lausanne is a city on Lake Geneva in Switzerland.

clue.text: Boss accepting gold back in Gloucestershire town

indicators.note: accepting means the boss word takes the gold inside it

parts.note: a stud is a boss, a raised ornamental knob

indicators.note: back means the gold word is read in reverse

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: The boss takes back the gold in a Cotswold town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like an employer but is a raised knob. Gloucestershire is an English county in the west.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroud is a market town in Gloucestershire, England.
